title: What Is the Average Cost of a Haircut in Canada? A Practical 2026 Price Guide
description: How much does a haircut cost in Canada? Explore men’s haircut prices, fade and beard service costs, and what to budget for a haircut in Saskatoon.
html:
By House of Havana Barbershop | All prices in Canadian dollars

For a standard men’s haircut in Canada, budgeting around $30 to $60 before tax and tip is a useful starting point. Salon haircuts involving more length, shaping, and finishing can cost considerably more. The right budget depends on the service you book, the professional you choose, and what the appointment includes.

That $30 to $60 range is a practical estimate based on selected published Canadian service menus, rather than a measured national average. There is no single price that fairly represents everything from a quick clipper cut to a detailed restyle with a wash and blowout.

If you are comparing haircut prices in Canada, the most useful question is: What am I getting for the price, and does that service suit my hair?

Here is what to know about haircut prices in Canada, what affects the cost, and how to choose a service that fits your style and budget. If you are looking for a men’s haircut in Saskatoon, you will also find our House of Havana service prices below.

Understanding the average haircut price in Canada

A quick trim, a detailed skin fade, and a complete restyle are all haircuts, but they involve different amounts of work. That is why a single average can tell you less than a clear service description.

For a standard men’s haircut, use $30 to $60 as an initial planning range. Some providers charge less, while specialist services, senior professionals, and longer appointments can cost more. This range reflects selected published menus reviewed for this guide, rather than a representative national survey.

When a menu says “from” or includes a “+” beside a price, treat that figure as a starting point. Your final quote may depend on the barber, your hair length, or the service required. Confirm the details before your appointment begins.

How much does a men’s haircut cost in Canada?

For someone booking a conventional barbershop haircut, a $30 to $60 starting budget provides a useful reference. It should not be treated as a minimum or maximum: some businesses charge less, while senior specialists and longer appointments may cost more.

A men’s haircut can also mean very different things. Maintaining an existing short style, rebuilding the shape of a grown-out haircut, and creating a skin fade with a textured top are separate tasks, even if a booking menu groups them under one heading.

Before booking, check:

  • Whether the service covers your desired style and current hair length.
  • Whether washing, drying, and styling are included.
  • Whether your chosen barber has a different rate.
  • Whether a restyle requires a longer appointment.
  • Whether beard work is included or booked separately.

Clear service descriptions make it easier to understand the value of the appointment and avoid choosing a shorter service that cannot accommodate the result you want.

What about women’s haircuts and longer salon appointments?

Because the question “What is the average cost of a haircut in Canada?” includes more than barber services, salon pricing deserves its own comparison.

The salon menus reviewed for this guide included women’s cuts from around $50 to $90, with some prices marked as starting rates. This is a snapshot of selected services, rather than a national average or an upper limit. Longer or more involved appointments may cost more.

Hair length, density, the amount of reshaping, finishing time, and stylist level can all affect the quote. Some businesses use gendered menus, while others organize appointments by length, time, or technique. Select the service that matches the work your hair needs, and ask if you are unsure.

Colour, highlights, chemical treatments, and extensions should be compared separately from haircut-only prices.

Why do haircut prices vary so much?

1. The haircut requires different techniques

A single-length buzz cut and a scissor cut with carefully balanced layers involve different work. A skin fade adds another set of decisions: how high the shortest section sits, how the transition blends, and how the sides connect with the top.

Detail matters around the crown, temples, neckline, and weight of the haircut. A style can look clean from the front yet feel bulky from the side or become difficult to manage after washing. Choosing a professional familiar with your intended result helps make the appointment more useful.

2. The appointment includes different services

One shop may list a haircut alone. Another may include a shampoo, conditioning treatment, styling, and a hot towel. Those prices are not directly equivalent.

Ask whether the listed price includes washing, drying, styling, and any finishing touches that matter to you. A slightly higher price may cover services that another menu charges for separately.

Comparing those details helps you understand the total cost before you book.

3. The professional has a different rate

Some barbershops and salons charge by barber or stylist level. A professional with extensive experience, specialist training, or strong demand may have a higher rate.

Price alone does not prove whether someone is the right fit. Look for relevant work: scissor cuts if you wear longer hair, controlled blending if you want a fade, or examples of your hair texture if that has been difficult to manage in the past.

4. The business operates in a different market

Rent, staffing, equipment, supplies, and the cost of maintaining a professional space contribute to what a business needs to charge. Location can influence these costs, but it is too simplistic to assume every haircut in one city costs more than every haircut in another.

Neighbourhood, service model, and appointment inclusions can matter as much as the city name.

How much does a skin fade cost?

A skin fade is not automatically a separate price category. Some barbers include it in their standard haircut rate; others offer a specific fade appointment.

At House of Havana, fades are booked under Haircut + Wash and Style, {{fadePrice}}. Ask your barber for your preferred fade when booking. The final price depends on the barber; this is our published starting rate, rather than an average Canadian skin fade price.

When booking a fade haircut, describe both the sides and the top. “Low skin fade with enough length on top to brush back” communicates more than “short on the sides.” A reference photo can help explain the finish you want, especially when paired with a conversation about your own hair density and growth pattern.

You can explore House of Havana’s haircut and fade services before choosing an appointment.

How much does a haircut and beard trim cost?

A haircut and beard appointment involves more work than a haircut alone. Beard grooming can include adjusting length, balancing the shape, refining the cheek line, and defining the neckline.

House of Havana’s Haircut + Beard Grooming service starts {{haircutBeardPrice}}. Allow {{haircutBeardDuration}}, depending on the barber and appointment selected.

Be careful when comparing a quick beard tidy with a full shaping service. They may differ in scope even when both appear under “beard trim.” Ask what is included, particularly if you want substantial reshaping or a razor finish.

Booking both services together also gives the barber an opportunity to consider how the haircut and beard connect around the sideburns and overall silhouette.

What does a men’s haircut cost in Saskatoon?

Is $50 expensive for a haircut in Canada?

A $50 men’s haircut falls within the practical planning range discussed in this guide. Whether it feels worthwhile depends on the result, the service, and your budget.

Useful signs of value include a clear consultation, a shape that suits your hair, careful finishing, and practical guidance on maintaining the style. Consistency matters too: being able to explain what you want and receive a dependable result can make regular grooming easier.

An affordable haircut can be excellent. A higher price also needs to be supported by a service you find valuable. Choose based on the work and experience you need rather than assuming that either the lowest or highest price is automatically the best choice.

How often should you get a haircut?

Your haircut schedule changes your overall grooming budget. As a starting point for discussion with your barber, consider:

  • A very sharp skin fade: a refresh roughly every two to three weeks if you want to preserve a closely maintained finish.
  • A classic short haircut or taper: roughly every three to five weeks, depending on how it grows out.
  • A medium-length scissor cut: roughly every four to six weeks, adjusted to the shape you want to maintain.
  • A longer hairstyle: agree on a schedule based on your growth goals and how the shape is holding up.

These are suggested planning intervals, not rules. Your hair growth, preferred finish, and willingness to style it matter more than a fixed calendar.

Tell your barber if you want a cut that can grow out comfortably between visits. That preference can influence how much length and weight they leave in different areas.

How much should you budget for haircuts each year?

To estimate your annual haircut spending, multiply the service price by the number of visits you plan to make.

For a hypothetical $50 haircut:

Booking scheduleApproximate visits per yearAnnual service cost
Every two weeks26$1,300
Every four weeks13$650
Every six weeks9$450

These examples exclude tax, optional tips, products, and extra services. They also show why a four-week schedule creates about 13 visits a year, rather than 12.

When comparing grooming options, consider the whole routine. The haircut price matters, but so do travel time, appointment availability, styling effort, and how often you want a refresh.

Does the haircut price include tax and tip?

Do not assume that the displayed service price is the final checkout total. Confirm whether applicable taxes are included and whether any additional services will change the price.

If you choose to leave a tip, include it separately in your personal budget. For example, on a $50 service, a tip calculated as 15% of the service price is $7.50, while 20% is $10. These are calculation examples, not required amounts.

If you are working within a firm budget, asking for the expected total before the appointment begins is entirely reasonable.

How to choose a barbershop that fits your budget

Start by finding work that resembles the result you want. A barber’s portfolio can help you assess their experience with fades, longer styles, textured hair, or beard shaping.

Next, read the booking description. Check the appointment length, service inclusions, barber rate, and any conditions attached to a starting price. Reviews can add context when they describe communication, consistency, and the experience across repeat visits.

Finally, explain what matters to you. You might want a polished business haircut that takes very little effort in the morning, a detailed skin fade, or a longer cut that you can continue growing. Clear expectations help the barber recommend the appropriate appointment.

A good consultation should also make room for your budget and maintenance preferences.

Frequently asked questions about haircut prices in Canada

What is the average cost of a haircut in Canada?

For a standard men’s haircut, around $30 to $60 before tax and tip is a practical starting budget based on the selected menus reviewed for this guide. It is an indicative range, not a statistically measured national average. Salon cuts, restyles, and specialist appointments can cost more.

Are haircuts cheaper at a barbershop or salon?

It depends on the service and provider. A basic barber service may cost less than a longer salon appointment, but premium barber services can overlap with salon pricing. Compare equivalent services and inclusions.

Why does my barber charge more for a skin fade?

Some businesses allocate different time or pricing to detailed fade work. Others include fades within their regular haircut service. Check the menu rather than assuming every shop follows the same system.

Is a wash included in the haircut price?

Sometimes. Published menus vary: some include washing and styling, while others list a haircut without shampoo. Confirm before booking if that is important to you.

Are children’s haircuts always cheaper?

No. Some businesses offer a reduced children’s rate, while others use the same price structure or charge according to the stylist. Check the age limits and service description.
